messages:
maria: Quick RFC follow-up — thinking through opaque vs JWT tradeoffs and a migration approach. Proposing a hybrid: short-lived JWTs for S2S, opaque long-lived for user API keys. Opinions?

kevin: JWTs are nice for offline validation at the gateway, but revocation is a pain unless we add jti+revocation list. Also key rotation needs KMS/HSM support and kid header handling.

sam: +1 for hybrid. Implementation idea: issue short-lived JWT (5m) and a refresh-style opaque token stored server-side for services that need longer sessions. For user API keys keep opaque with project binding metadata.

priya: From product POV customers often want one project-level key, but requests for per-route keys for billing and least privilege come up. How would we express that in scopes?

luca: If JWT includes actor_id and project_id claims it makes tracing and audits easier. But must ensure service tokens can't escalate to org-level by forging claims. Enforce token issuance checks at mint time.

kevin: Implementation details: token-service signs JWTs using KMS (HSM-backed). Use kid and rotate keys. Include jti in JWT; maintain a small revocation table for jti so we can emergency-revoke. For routine revocation of long-lived opaque keys we keep DB rows + index by key_id.

sam: Introspection cost note — gateway should cache introspection results per-token for a short TTL (30s?) and subscribe to a pubsub revocation topic so cache can be invalidated quickly on revokes. Avoid pulling introspection on every request.

maria: Migration plan sketch: accept v1 opaque tokens for compatibility and v2 hybrid tokens. For ~8 weeks accept both; v2 tokens will have explicit "scope" claims like "project:123:write". Legacy tokens map to a project default or org default for backward compatibility.

priya: Compliance/enterprise ask: we need minting audit logs: who requested the token, reason, machine identity, and policy that allowed issuance. Add audit fields to ticket.

kevin: DB migration note: tokens table needs columns: token_type, kid, jti, expires_at, actor_id, project_id, scopes (jsonb). Backfill: existing opaque -> token_type=opaque, infer project_id from owner mapping. Will require a maintenance window for indexing.

luca: Rollout plan: start internal-only, flip on for internal services, then open to customer tenants. Gateway needs to support dual acceptance (opaque introspection + JWT local validation) for the transition window. @sam can you take gateway work?

sam: I got it. Plan: add JWT validation path in gateway, keep introspect path, add caching + pubsub invalidate. Canary route first. ETA 2w for prototype, 4w for canary. Need infra help for load tests.

maria: Action items:
- sam: gateway dual-accept + cache + canary
- kevin: token-service jti+revocation API + KMS key rotation, DB schema change
- priya: product docs + opt-in per-route key UX + enterprise audit requirements
- luca: alerts for revocation spikes, audit retention policy
Please create tickets and assign owners.

kevin: I'll open infra PR for KMS keys and a migration ticket for the tokens table. Will add PR template notes for rollbacks.

priya: I'll draft the docs and a short customer comms plan for opt-in per-route keys. Also adding a support playbook for token revocation incidents.

maria: Final question — impersonation. Separate token type or claim? I'm leaning separate impersonation tokens minted via admin flow with an "act_as" claim and very short TTL.

kevin: separate token type + stricter minting (MFA admin approval or signed operator flow). Keep TTL <= 10m and require audit_reason.

maria: Perfect. Thanks everyone. I'll consolidate this into a short RFC follow-up with the migration timetable. :thumbsup:

auth-bot: token-service v0.9 deployed to staging (build 2025.11.3) — introspection endpoint available for testing.

luca: noted, will run a smoke test against staging introspect endpoint today.

maria: ok closing thread — will post the RFC follow-up doc link when done.
